explanation: Retain both the largest and smallest products ending at the previous value. Multiplication by a negative number can swap their roles; compare both extensions with starting a new subarray.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Every subarray ending at the current position either starts there or extends one ending immediately before it. A negative multiplier can turn the previous minimum into the new maximum, so retaining both extrema covers all candidates. The greatest ending maximum across positions is the optimum over all nonempty subarrays.
walkthrough: For [-2,3,-4,0,2], products ending at 3 include -6 and 3. Multiplying the previous minimum -6 by -4 yields 24, from subarray [-2,3,-4]. Zero resets later products and the final 2 is smaller, so return 24.
edgeCases: Zero can separate otherwise unrelated product ranges.
Both maximum and minimum ending products are needed for negative values.
